title: The Night Owl — a sleeper-train landing page
description: A landing page for The Night Owl, an invented overnight sleeper line from Harrowgate Central to Port Aurelia. It opens on a canvas night landscape in which the lit train holds the frame while ridges, pines and telegraph poles slide past. Below that are a cabin comparison, a route timeline with a clock you can drag to follow the train through the night, a seeded berth map with live pricing and a ten-minute hold that counts down and expires, and an FAQ.
prompt: Design a luxurious landing page for a fictional overnight sleeper train. Invent the company and a route between fictional-but-plausible stops, and don't make it look like any real operator. I want a cinematic parallax night landscape with a train passing, a cabin class comparison, an interactive route timeline with stops and times, a berth picker seat map where I can select berths, hold them and see a price total, and an FAQ. Art-deco elegance, brass on midnight, and honest about being fictional.

methodology: Timetable oracle: the scrubber's position is checked against hand-computed interpolation, e.g. 01:00 is 10 of the 140 minutes between Coldwater Junction (dep 00:50) and Ashby Ridge (arr 03:10), giving 214 + 10/140 × 104 ≈ 221 miles. Dwell time at a station reads 'Standing at …'.

Pricing oracle: totals are recomputed from the published fares plus the $12 per-berth fee, including a 15% weekend supplement on Friday departures, and selections are cleared when the departure changes.
Time control: page.clock is installed on a fixed Tuesday so the date list and weekday/weekend fares are deterministic, and fastForward drives the ten-minute hold through 6:00, 0:01 and expiry.
State-machine checks for the hold: while held, the chosen berths show as held, every other berth and the date select are locked, and releasing or expiring restores everything.
Seeded availability (?seed=) makes the taken berths repeatable; the spec reads them from window.__owl and asserts they are disabled in the DOM.
Visual review of the canvas hero at 1280 and 390 px, including the moon placement on narrow screens and a forced headline break.
risks: The hold countdown uses setInterval and Date.now(); a background tab could skip ticks, so expiry is based on the deadline timestamp, not on counting ticks.
Timetable times cross midnight; times are converted to minutes since the 20:15 departure to avoid wrap-around bugs.
The hero's rAF loop costs battery; it stops when the tab is hidden and, under reduced motion, redraws only on scroll or resize.
Seat-map grids on 360px phones; roomettes drop to four columns and cabins to two.
qa.playwright: page.clock does most of the work: install() plus pauseAt() fixes 'today' so the ten-night date list and the weekend supplement are deterministic, and fastForward('04:00') / ('09:59') / ('00:02') checks the countdown text at exact moments and then the expiry, without any real waiting. Seeded berth availability is read from window.__owl.taken rather than hard-coded, so the test remains valid if the seat layout changes. The canvas hero is decorative and marked aria-hidden, so it is not asserted in the spec; it was reviewed from screenshots. The 'choose a cabin' jump runs under emulateMedia reducedMotion so the focus handoff happens immediately and can be asserted with a :focus locator.
coverage: Cabin fares, feature matrix and the jump to the matching car with focus
Stop details (dwell times, dimmed-lamps badge) and aria-pressed selection
Scrubber at departure, dwell, mid-segment, mileage and arrival
Seeded taken berths, selection, totals, fees, weekend supplement, four-berth cap
Ten-minute hold: countdown, locking, release and expiry under page.clock
FAQ disclosure and the fictional-railway disclaimer

a11y: Stops and berths are real buttons with aria-pressed. Each berth has a full aria-label giving car, berth, price and state; taken and locked berths are disabled. The scrubber is a labelled range whose position text and the stop details are aria-live, the booking messages are announced, the FAQ uses native details/summary, and the canvas hero is aria-hidden.
